उप मिाजनिेिक (खान सुरक्षा), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (खनन), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (खनन), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (जिद्युत), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (जिद्युत), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा सिायक जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), िजक्षण-पूिी क्षेत्र । िजक्षण पूिी िोन जिसका अजधकाररता ओजडिा राज्य और झारखंड के कुछ भाग में िै जिसका मुख्यालय रांची (झारखंड) में िै, जिसमें रांची क्षेत्र, चाईबासा क्षेत्र, भुिनेश्वर क्षेत्र-1 और भुिनेश्वर क्षेत्र-2 िाजमल िैं। 5.
उप मिाजनिेिक (खान सुरक्षा), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (खनन), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (खनन), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र। खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (जिद्युत), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (जिद्युत), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा सिायक जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), िजक्षण-मध्य क्षेत्र । िजक्षण मध्य क्षेत्र जिसका अजधकाररता तेलंगाना और आंध्र प्रिेि राज्यों में िै, जिसका मुख्यालय िैिराबाि (तेलंगाना) में िै, जिसमें िैिराबाि क्षेत्र- 1, िैिराबाि क्षेत्र-2, िैिराबाि क्षेत्र-3 और नेल्लोर क्षेत्र िाजमल िैं। 6.
उप मिाजनिेिक (खान सुरक्षा), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (खनन), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (खनन), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (जिद्युत), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (जिद्युत), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । िजक्षणी क्षेत्र जिसका अजधकाररता कनायटक, केरल, तजमलनाडु राज्यों और लक्षद्वीप द्वीप समूि और पुडुचेरी के संघ राज् य क्षेत्र में िै, जिसका मुख्यालय बेंगलुरू (कनायटक) में िै, जिसमें बेंगलुरु क्षेत्र, बेल्लारी क्षेत्र-1, बेल्लारी क्षेत्र-2 और चेन्नई क्षेत्र िाजमल िैं। THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)]
खान सुरक्षा सिायक जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), िजक्षणी क्षेत्र । 7.
उप मिाजनिेिक (खान सुरक्षा), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (खनन), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (खनन), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), पजिमी क्षेत्र। खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (जिद्युत), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (जिद्युत), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा सिायक जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), पजिमी क्षेत्र । पजिमी क्षेत्र जिसका अजधकाररता मिाराष्ट्र, छत्तीसगढ़ और गोिा राज्यों में िै, जिसका मुख्यालय नागपुर (मिाराष्ट्र) में िै, जिसमें नागपुर क्षेत्र-1, नागपुर क्षेत्र-2, जबलासपुर क्षेत्र-1, जबलासपुर क्षेत्र-2, रायगढ़ क्षेत्र और गोिा क्षेत्र िाजमल िैं। 8.
उप मिाजनिेिक (खान सुरक्षा), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र ।खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (खनन), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (खनन), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (जिद्युत), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (जिद्युत), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा सिायक जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), उत्तर-पजिमी क्षेत्र । उत्तर पजिमी क्षेत्र जिसका अजधकाररता गुिरात, रािस्ट्थान राज्यों और िमन, िािरा और नगर ििेली और िीि संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों में िै, जिसका मुख्यालय उियपुर (रािस्ट्थान) में िै, जिसमें अिमिाबाि क्षेत्र-1, अिमिाबाि क्षेत्र-2, सूरत क्षेत्र, उियपुर क्षेत्र, अिमेर क्षेत्र-1 और अिमेर क्षेत्र-2 िाजमल िैं। 9.
उप मिाजनिेिक (खान सुरक्षा), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (खनन), उत्तरी क्षेत्र। खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (खनन), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (यांजत्रक), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक (जिद्युत), उत्तरी क्षेत्र। खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (जिद्युत), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । उत्तरी क्षेत्र जिसका अजधकाररता उत्तर प्रिेि, िररयाणा, उत्तराखंड, जिमाचल प्रिेि, पंिाब, मध्य प्रिेि और दिल्ली, चंडीगढ़, िम्मू और कश्मीर और लदाखाख संघ राज् य क्षेत्र में िै, जिसका मुख्यालय गाजियाबाि (उत्तर प्रिेि) में िै, जिसमें गाजियाबाि क्षेत्र, श्रीनगर क्षेत्र, पराजसया क्षेत्र, िबलपुर क्षेत्र, ग्िाजलयर क्षेत्र और िाराणसी क्षेत्र िाजमल िैं। [भाग II—खण् ड 3(ii)]
भारत का रािपत्र : असाधारण खान सुरक्षा सिायक जनिेिक (व्यािसाजयक स्ट्िास्ट््य), उत्तरी क्षेत्र । 10.
धनबाि क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। झारखंड राज्य का जिस्ट्सा: धनबाि जिले की सभी खिानें जगररडीि-टुंडी- गोविंिपुर रोड के पजिम में और गोविंिपुर-धनबाि से बोकारो तक राष्ट्रीय रािमागय -32 के उत्तर में जस्ट्थत िैं। 11.
धनबाि क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। झारखंड राज्य का जिस्ट्सा: धनबाि जिले की सभी खिानें जगररडीि-टुंडी- गोविंिपुर रोड के पूिय में और गोविंिपुर-धनबाि से बोकारो तक राष्ट्रीय रािमागय -32 के िजक्षण में जस्ट्थत िैं। 12.
धनबाि क्षेत्र-3 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। झारखंड राज्य का जिस्ट्सा: िामताडा, िेिघर, िुमका, पाकुड, गोड्डा और सािेबगंि जिलों में सभी खान। 13.
कोडरमा क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। जबिार राज्य और झारखंड का जिस्ट्सा: जबिार राज्य की सभी खानें और झारखंड राज्य के कोडरमा, जगररडीि और बोकारो जिलों में सभी खानें। 14.
जसतारामपुर क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। पजिमी बंगाल राज्य का जिस्ट्सा: पजिम (पजिम) बियिान जिले की सभी खानें राष्ट्रीय रािमागय -2 के िजक्षण में जस्ट्थत िैं। पुरुजलया, बांकुरा, झारग्राम, पजिम (पजिम), मेदिनीपुर और पूिय (पूिय)
मेदिनीपुर जिलों की सभी खानें.
15.
जसतारामपुर क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। पजिमी बंगाल राज्य का भाग : राष्ट्रीय रािमागय-2 के उत्तर में तथा राष्ट्रीय रािमागय-2 पर जस्ट्थत पंिाबी मोड से पांडिेश्वर घाट तक िाने िाले राष्ट्रीय रािमागय-60 के पूिय में जस्ट्थत पजिम बधयमान जिले की समस्ट्त खानें। पूिय बधयमान, मुर्ियिाबाि, नदिया, उत्तर 24 परगना, िजक्षण 24 परगना, िािडा, हुगली, कोलकाता, मालिा, िजक्षण दिनािपुर, उत्तर दिनािपुर, िार्ियवलंग, िलपाईगुडी, अलीपुरद्वार, कूच जबिार तथा काजलम्पोंग जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। अंडमान एिं जनकोबार द्वीपसमूि संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : समस्ट्त खानें। 16.
जसतारामपुर क्षेत्र-3 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। पजिमी बंगाल राज्य का भाग: राष्ट्रीय रािमागय 2 के उत्तर में तथा राष्ट्रीय रािमागय 2 पर जस्ट्थत पंिाबी मोड से पांडिेश्वर घाट तक िाने िाले राष्ट्रीय रािमागय-60 के पजिम में जस्ट्थत पजिम बधयमान जिले की समस्ट्त खानें। बीरभूम जिले की समस्ट्त खानें। 17.
गुिािाटी क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। असम, जसदिम, अरुणाचल प्रिेि, मजणपुर, जमिोरम, मेघालय, नागालैंड तथा जत्रपुरा राज्यों की समस्ट्त खानें। 18.
रांची क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। झारखंड राज्य का भाग : रांची, रामगढ़, िजारीबाग, चतरा, पलामू तथा गढ़िा जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)]
19.
चाईबासा क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। झारखंड राज्य का भाग : पूिी वसंिभूम, पजिमी वसंिभूम, सरायकेला- खरसािां, गुमला, खूंटी, जसमडेगा, लातेिार तथा लोिरिगा जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 20.
भुिनेश्वर क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। ओजडिा राज्य का भाग : अंगुल, ढेंकानाल, िािपुर, क्योंझर (केंिुझार), भरक, बालासोर (बालेश्वर), केंरापडा, िगतवसंिपुर, कटक, खुिाय, पुरी, नयागढ़, गंिाम, गिपजत तथा मयूरभंि जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 21.
भुिनेश्वर क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। ओजडिा राज्य का भाग : सुंिरगढ़, झारसुगुडा, संबलपुर, िेिगढ़ (िेबगढ़), बौध, बरगढ़, सुिणयपुर (सोनपुर), नुआपाडा, बलांगीर, कंधमाल (फूलबनी), रायगढ़ा, कालािांडी, नबरंगपुर, कोरापुट तथा मलकानजगरर जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 22.
िैिराबाि क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। तेलंगाना राज्य का भाग : खम्मम, करीमनगर, िनुमकोंडा, िारंगल, मिबूबाबाि, भरारी कोठागुडेम, ियिंकर-भूपालपल्ली, मुलुगु, िनगांि, जसजिपेट, मिबूबनगर, िनपती, िोगुलाम्बा-गडिाल, नारायणपेट, सूयायपेट, यािारी-भुिनजगरर, मेडचल-मलकािजगरर, रंगारेड्डी, िैिराबाि, नलगोंडा तथा नागरकनूयल जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 23.
िैिराबाि क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। तेलंगाना राज्य का भाग : आदिलाबाि, मंचेररयल, जनमयल, कुमारम भीम, जनिामाबाि, पेदाखापल्ली, रािन्ना-जसरजसल्ला, कामारेड्डी, मेडक, संगारेड्डी, िजगत्याल तथा जिकाराबाि जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 24.
िैिराबाि क्षेत्र-3 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। आंध्र प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : पजिम गोिािरी, पूिय गोिािरी, कृष्णा, काकीनाडा, डॉ. बी.आर. अम्बेडकर कोनसीमा, एलुरु, अल्लूरी सीताराम रािू, गुंटूर, पलनाडु, बापटला, जििाखापत्तनम, जिियनगरम, श्रीकाकुलम, प्रकािम, कुरनूल, नंद्याल, अनकापल्ली, पाियतीपुरम मन्द्यम तथा एन.टी.आर. जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 25.
नेल्लोर क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। आंध्र प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : श्री पोरि श्रीरामुलु नेल्लोर, िाई.एस.आर., जचत्तूर, अनंतपुरम, अन्नमय्या, जतरुपजत तथा श्री सत्यसाई जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 26.
बेंगलुरु क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। कनायटक राज्य का भाग : जचकमगलूर, िजक्षण कन्नड, जचत्रिुगय, तुमकुरु, िासन, कोलार, बेंगलुरु ििरी, बेंगलुरु ग्रामीण, मांड्या, मैसूर (मैसूरु), चामरािनगर, कोडगु, रामनगर, जचिबल्लापुर, िािणगेरे, जििमोग्गा तथा उडुपी जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। केरल राज्य तथा लक्षद्वीप द्वीपसमूि संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : समस्ट्त खानें। 27.
बेल्लारी क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। कनायटक राज्य का भाग : बल्लारी (बेल्लारी), जिियनगर, रायचूर (रायचुरु), यािजगरर, कलबुगी (गुलबगाय) तथा बीिर जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 28.
बेल्लारी क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। कनायटक राज्य का भाग : जिियपुरा (बीिापुर), बागलकोट, गडग, कोप्पल, बेलगािी (बेलगाम), धारिाड, िािेरी तथा उत्तर कन्नड जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। [भाग II—खण् ड 3(ii)]
भारत का रािपत्र : असाधारण 29.
चेन्नई क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। तजमलनाडु राज्य : समस्ट्त खानें। पुिुचेरी संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : समस्ट्त खानें। 30.
नागपुर क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। मिाराष्ट्र राज्य का भाग : गोंदिया, भंडारा, नागपुर, िधाय, अमरािती, अकोला, बुलढाणा, िालना, विंगोली, परभणी, औरंगाबाि, िाजिम तथा गढ़जचरौली जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 31.
नागपुर क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। मिाराष्ट्र राज्य का भाग : चंरपुर, यितमाल, नांिेड, लातूर, बीड तथा उस्ट्मानाबाि जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 32.
जबलासपुर क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। छत्तीसगढ़ राज्य का भाग : कोरबा, रायपुर, गररयाबंि, बलौिाबाजार- भाटापारा, धमतरी, बस्ट्तर, कोंडागांि तथा सुकमा जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 33.
जबलासपुर क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। छत्तीसगढ़ राज्य का भाग : कोररया, भरतपुर-मनेन्द्रगढ़-जचरजमरी, जबलासपुर, मुंगेली, किधाय (कबीरधाम), िुगय, रािनांिगांि, खैरागढ़- छुईखिान-गंडई, मोिला-मानपुर-चौकी, बालोि, बेमेतरा, कांकेर, नारायणपुर, िंतेिाडा, बीिापुर तथा गौरेला-पेंड्रा-मरिािी जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 34.
रायगढ़ क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। छत्तीसगढ़ राज्य का भाग : रायगढ़, सारंगढ़-जबलाईगढ़, ििपुर, सरगुिा, सूरिपुर, बलरामपुर, िांिगीर-चांपा, सिी तथा मिासमुंि जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 35.
गोिा क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। गोिा राज्य : गोिा राज्य की समस्ट्त खानें। मिाराष्ट्र राज्य का भाग : अिमिनगर, नंिुरबार, मुंबई, मुंबई उपनगरीय, ठाणे, पालघर, नाजसक, धुले, िलगांि, सतारा, रत्नाजगरर, सांगली, कोल्िापुर, सोलापुर, वसंधुिुगय, रायगढ़ तथा पुणे जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 36.
अिमिाबाि क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। गुिरात राज्य का भाग : िामनगर, िेिभूजम द्वारका, पोरबंिर, रािकोट, मोरबी, िूनागढ़, जगर-सोमनाथ, अमरेली, भािनगर, अिमिाबाि तथा बोटाि जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। िीि संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : समस्ट्त खानें। 37.
अिमिाबाि क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। गुिरात राज्य का भाग : गांधीनगर, मिेसाणा, पाटन, कच्छ, मिीसागर, सुरेन्द्रनगर, बनासकांठा, साबरकांठा तथा अरिल्ली जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 38.
सूरत क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। गुिरात राज्य का भाग : पंचमिल, िािोि, िडोिरा, छोटा उियपुर, भरूच, नमयिा, सूरत, निसारी, तापी, िलसाड, डांग, आनंि तथा खेडा जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। िमन तथा िािरा और नगर ििेली संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : िमन तथा िािरा और नगर ििेली की समस्ट्त खानें। 39.
उियपुर क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। रािस्ट्थान राज्य का भाग : रािसमंि, उियपुर, डूंगरपुर, बांसिाडा, प्रतापगढ़, जचत्तौडगढ़, जसरोिी तथा िालौर जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)]
40.
अिमेर क्षेत्र-1 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। रािस्ट्थान राज्य का भाग : ियपुर, अिमेर, िौसा, सिाई माधोपुर, टोंक, बूंिी, भरतपुर, अलिर, कोटा, भीलिाडा, बारां, झालािाड, करौली तथा धौलपुर जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 41.
अिमेर क्षेत्र-2 के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। रािस्ट्थान राज्य का भाग : िोधपुर, बाडमेर, िैसलमेर, बीकानेर, श्रीगंगानगर, िनुमानगढ़, पाली, नागौर, चूरू, झुंझुनूं तथा सीकर जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 42.
गाजियाबाि क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। उत्तर प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : मुिफ्फरनगर, िामली, सिारनपुर, जबिनौर, मेरठ, िापुड, बागपत, गाजियाबाि, बुलंिििर, गौतम बुि नगर, ज्योजतबा फुले नगर (अमरोिा), मुरािाबाि, रामपुर, अलीगढ़, बिायूं, संभल (भीमनगर), बरेली, पीलीभीत, मथुरा, िाथरस, एटा, कांिीराम नगर (कासगंि), िािििांपुर, लखीमपुर खीरी, आगरा, दफरोिाबाि, मैनपुरी, फरुयखाबाि, िरिोई, सीतापुर, इटािा, कन्नौि, औरैया, कानपुर नगर, कानपुर िेिात, उन्नाि, लखनऊ, िालौन, झांसी, लजलतपुर, िमीरपुर तथा मिोबा जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। िररयाणा, उत्तराखंड राज्य तथा दिल्ली संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : समस्ट्त खानें। 43.
श्रीनगर क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। िम्मू और कश्मीर, लदाखाख तथा चंडीगढ़ संघ राज्य क्षेत्र : समस्ट्त खानें। जिमाचल प्रिेि तथा पंिाब राज्य : समस्ट्त खानें। 44.
पराजसया क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। मध्य प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : वछंििाडा, बैतूल, जसिनी, बालाघाट, मंडला, नमयिापुरम (िोिंगाबाि), नरवसंिपुर तथा िरिा जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 45.
िबलपुर क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। मध्य प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : रीिा, सतना, पन्ना, िमोि, कटनी, उमररया, ििडोल, अनूपपुर, िबलपुर तथा रायसेन जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 46.
ग्िाजलयर क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। मध्य प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : मुरैना, श्योपुर, वभंड, ग्िाजलयर, जििपुरी, गुना, भोपाल, जिदििा, िजतया, रािगढ़, टीकमगढ़, छतरपुर, अिोकनगर, सागर, सीिोर, झाबुआ, अलीरािपुर, धार, खरगोन, खंडिा, बडिानी, बुरिानपुर, नीमच, मंिसौर, रतलाम, उज्जैन, िािापुर, आगर मालिा, िेिास, इंिौर, जनिाडी तथा वडंडोरी जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। 47.
िाराणसी क्षेत्र के खान सुरक्षा जनिेिक, खान सुरक्षा उप जनिेिक। उत्तर प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : बिराइच, श्रािस्ट्ती, बाराबंकी, गोंडा, रायबरेली, फतेिपुर, बांिा, जचत्रकूट, कौिांबी, प्रतापगढ़, सुल्तानपुर, अमेठी, अयोध्या (फैिाबाि), बस्ट्ती, बलरामपुर, जसिाथयनगर, मिारािगंि, संत कबीर नगर, अंबेडकर नगर, िौनपुर, प्रयागराि, कुिीनगर, िेिररया, गोरखपुर, आिमगढ़, मऊ, बजलया, संत रजििास नगर (भिोिी), िाराणसी, जमिायपुर, चंिौली, सोनभर तथा गािीपुर जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। मध्य प्रिेि राज्य का भाग : सीधी तथा वसंगरौली (िैढन) जिलों की समस्ट्त खानें। [फा. सं. एस-65025/8/2026-आईएसएच-II]

title: Safety measures for trucks, tippers, dumpers and OTR tyre handling
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 05 of 2026 — Safety measures for trucks, tippers, dumpers and OTR tyre handling
text:
æRQ5R/Government of India Ministry of Labour & Employment Directorate General of Mines Safety BRICs DGMS (Tech) Circular No. /MHQ/2026/ 05 To, Dhanbad, Date 04/ 2026 All Owners, Agent and Managers of Coal and Metalliferous mines Subject: Strengthening Safety Measures for Trucks, Tippers, Dumpers and OTR Tyre Handling Operations in Mines.
I invite your attention to the alarming increase in accidents involving Wheeled Trackless Transportation Machinery, specifically dumper, tippers, trucks and similar vehicles etc., deployed in mines.
The analysis of accident statistics in coal and Metalliferous mines for the year 2023 to 2025 revealed that a total of 118 and 94 fatal accidents occurred involving 142 and 125 fatalities in coal and Metalliferous mines respectively. Out of the total, 39 (33%) fatal accidents involving 42 fatalities in coal and 21 (22%) fatal accidents involving 26 fatalities in metalliferous mines were related to transport machinery such as dumpers, tippers, trucks and other wheeled trackless vehicles.
In the year 2026(till 31st July, 2026), a total of 25 fatal accidents occurred in coal mines involving 26 fatalities and 25 fatal accidents occurred in Metalliferous mines involving 31 fatalities. Out of the total 9 (36%) fatal accidents involving 9 fatalities in coal and 8 (32%) fatal accidents involving 8 fatalities in metalliferous mines were related to transport machinery such as dumpers, tippers, trucks and other wheeled trackless vehicles It has further been noticed that, in last three years 4 fatal accidents and 5 dangerouS occurrences had taken place during handling, removal, mounting and dismantling of large off the road (OTR) tyres due to the use of tyre handlers without essential safety devices, improper operating procedures, inadequate maintenance and insufficient training of operators.
From the analysis of above accidents revealed that, most of the fatal accidents due to transportation vehicle caused due to run-over and/or toppling of wheeled trackless equipment and/or during tyre handling, etc., in coal and Metalliferous mines.
The analysis further revealed that all the above accidents could have been averted had the precautions & preventive measures as prescribed in the statute, circulars, guidelines issued by the Directorate from time to time had been taken.
It has been observed with serious concern that fatal and serious accidents involving trucks, tippers and dumpers continue to occur in mines despite the enforcement of G.S.R. 987(E) dated 01.10.2018 issued under Regulation 216(2) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017, prescribing mandatory safety features and devices for Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM). Recent DGMS(Tech.) circulars no. 06 of 2020 and 07 of 2025 and DGMS safety alerts also indicate that accidents involving wheeled trackless transportation machinery remain a major cause of fatalities in opencast mines.(both in Coal and Metalliferous mines)
Accordingly, all Owners, Agents and Managers of mines are hereby directed to ensure the following:
1. No truck, tipper or dumper shall be deployed unless all safety features specified under G.S.R. 987(E) are installed, periodically tested and functioning properly.
2. Daily pre-operational inspection of braking systems, steering, seat belts, reversing alarms, lighting, cameras, blind-spot monitoring, proximity warning systems and other mandatory safety devices shall be carried out and recorded.
3. Defective HEMM shall be withdrawn from service immediately until all defects affecting safety are rectified.
4. All persons employed or to be employed to operate heavy earth moving machinery including tippers and dumpers shall be trained and their competency shall be evaluated by a Board constituted by the management, who shall be the persons who are not connected with imparting training.
Training module for imparting special training to "operators" or "drivers" of wheeled trackless equipment shall be prepared based on the size, capacity, type, manufacturer, use, etc., of the equipment and considering original equipment manufacturer(OEM) modules/schedules on operation and maintenance.
5. Tyre handlers shall be fitted with all safety devices, including tyre fall back arrester , hydraulic cut-off of load moment indicator ,suitable gradeability.
overload protection, emergency stop systems, locking mechanisms and other fail-safe features.
6. Manual handling of large off the road (OTR) tyres shall be strictly prohibited wherever mechanical tyre handling equipment is available.
7. Risk assessment shall made on tyre handling and based on that Standard Operating Procedures (SOPS) shall be prepared and strictly implemented for all tyre handling and dismantling operations.
8. Only trained, competent and authorised persons shall be allowed to operate tyre handlers and carry out OTR tyre mounting or dismantling.
9. Periodic inspection, preventive maintenance and functional testing of tyre handlers shall be conducted and documented.
10. Mine management shall conduct regular safety audits to verify compliance with G.S.R. 987(E), haul road standards, traffic management plans and tyre handling procedures.
11. Any non-compliance observed during inspection shall be rectified immediately, and further preventive action shall be ensured.
All mine Owner, Agent and Managers are directed to review existing safety arrangements and take immediate corrective measures to prevent recurrence of such accidents. Strict compliance with statutory provisions, Circulars, guidelines, DGMS notifications and the recommendations contained in DGMS Safety Alerts shall be ensured at all times.
This circular shall be brought to the notice of all concerned officers, supervisors, operators, contractors and workmen and shall be displayed prominently at suitable locations in the mi e.
Direct ate General of Mines Safety & Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator

title: Submission of accurate and complete Annual Returns
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 06 of 2026 — Submission of accurate and complete Annual Returns
text:
of India Ministry of Labour & Employment Directorate General of Mines safety DGMS (Tech) Circular No. /CMC/2026/06 Dhanbad, Date 08-2026 To, All Owners, Agent and Managers of Coal, Metalliferous and Oil mines.
Subject: Submission of Accurate and Complete Annual Returns by Mine Managements.
It has been observed during scrutiny of the Annual Returns submitted by various mine managements that a large number of returns contain incomplete, incorrect, or inconsistent information. Such discrepancies adversely affect the quality and reliability of the national database relating to mines and hinder meaningful statistical analysis.
The Annual Returns submitted by mine managements constitute an important source of information for the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS). The data furnished therein are extensively utilized for monitoring safety and health performance, analysing accident and occupational disease trends, identifying emerging hazards, assessing the effectiveness of safety measures, and formulating evidence-based regulatory interventions and data driven decision making.
However, the scrutiny of Annual Returns has revealed the following common discrepancies:
1.
2.
3.
4.
5.
6.
7.
Incorrect or incomplete name of the owner.
Incorrect name of the company, including the use of abbreviations or short forms instead of the registered name.
Incorrect or incomplete address of the mine, particularly the district, State, and PIN code.
of the (Coal/Metalliferous/Oil, classification mine Incorrect Underground/Opencast/Mixed, etc.).
Incorrect entry regarding the gassiness classification of the seam, wherever applicable.
Mismatch between the figures of employment (manpower) and production reported.
Production reported whereas consumption of explosives has been shown as "Nil" or "Zero" despite blasting operations being carried out.
8.
9.
Horsepower (HP)/rated power of machinery and equipment deployed in the mine not furnished or incorrectly reported.
Incomplete or incorrect particulars relating to persons employed, including category-wise manpower, vocational training, refresher training, and initial/periodical medical examination.
10. Mismatch between production, dispatch, and stock figures.
11. Inconsistency in the number of working days, shifts worked, and production achieved.
12. Incomplete or inconsistent details of Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM), transport equipment, winding machinery, or other major machinery.
13. Incorrect or non-reporting of electricity consumption or other energy-related data.
14. Incorrect reporting of drilling, blasting, and explosive consumption details.
15. Non-reporting or incorrect reporting of accidents, dangerous occurrences, or occupational diseases.
16. Mismatch between the number of statutory officials employed and the manpower reported in the employment section.
17. Incorrect reporting of contract workers or omission of contract labour engaged in the mine.
18. Incorrect or incomplete reporting of mine closure, temporary discontinuance, or suspension of mining operations.
19. Inconsistent information regarding mine status (working, discontinued, abandoned, or under development).
20. Mandatory fields left blank or filled with default values such as "Nil", "N.A.", or "0" without proper justification.
21. Computational errors, inconsistent units of measurement, or incorrect totals in the submitted Annual Returns.
The above discrepancies seriously impair the reliability of statistical analysis carried out by DGMS. Inaccurate or inconsistent data lead to misleading trends in accident analysis, including accident rates per thousand persons employed, accident rates per million tonnes of production, accident trends based on the level of mechanisation, and analyses relating to drilling, blasting, and explosive consumption. Similar inaccuracies also affect the analysis of occupational diseases and other occupational health indicators.
Reliable analysis of accidents and occupational diseases is essential for identifying causative factors, emerging risks, and priority areas requiring regulatory attention.
Such analyses form the basis for framing or revising statutory provisions, issuing technical guidelines, circulars, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), advisories, and other preventive measures for improving safety and health standards in mines with the ultimate objective of achieving Zero Harm in line with vision Viksit Bharat, 2047.
Further, the information furnished through Annual Returns is utilized for compilation of official publications and reports, including:
DGMS Annual Report;
Statistics of Mines in India (Volume-I and Volume-II);
Ministry of Labour & Employment Annual Report;
Replies to Parliament Questions;
Reports submitted to the Ministry, other Government agencies, and national/international organizations; and Various statistical analyses and policy documents prepared by DGMS.
In view of the above, all Owners, Agents and Managers of mines are hereby advised to ensure that:
1. All Annual Returns are prepared carefully and submitted only after due verification of every entry and authenticated by Owner/Agent/Manager.
2. The information furnished is complete, accurate, internally consistent, and supported by authentic records maintained under the applicable statutory provisions.
3. Production, employment, dispatch, stock, machinery, explosives, electricity consumption, accidents, occupational diseases, and other operational data are cross-verified before submission.
4. Mandatory fields are not left blank or filled with default values such as "Nil", "N.A.", or "0" unless such entries are factually correct and duly justified.
5. Any discrepancy noticed after submission of the Annual Return is immediately brought to the notice of the concerned Regional Office of DGMS and corrected in accordance with the prescribed procedure.
All mine managements are advised to accord due importance to the accuracy and completeness of Annual Returns. Submission of incorrect, misleading, or incomplete information may invite appropriate action under the applicable provisions of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and the rules and regulations made thereunder.
(Ujjwal#ah)
Directorate General of Mines Safety & Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator

of India of Labour & Employment General of Mines safety EFßTZ/Dhanbad No. DGMS (Legislative) circular No. D L of 2026, Dhanbad, dated: 25 / 08/2026 To All Owners, Agent and Managers of coal, Metalliferous and oil mines Subject: Guidelines for preparation of training scheme.
The Central Government, in exercise of the powers conferred by the sub-section (2) of section 1 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (37 of 2020), appointed the 21st day of November, 2025 as the date on which the provisions of the said Code, have come into force [S.O. 5321(E)]
and subsequently Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026 come into force with effect from 08.05.2026. As required under Rule 157(1) of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, the guidelines for preparation of training scheme by the employer of every mine for persons employed or to be employed in the mine is specified as follow:- Scope:
This document specifies the guidelines for preparation of training scheme under Rule 157, for imparting training to the persons employed or to be employed in the mine under Rules 158, 159, 161, 162 and any other training under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, at a training center established under Rule 163 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026.
The training scheme shall include, amongst others, the following essential elements - 1.0 GENERAL:
1.1 The training scheme prepared by the employer of a mine or an employer nominated under Rule 163(2) shall contain detailed framework and modality for imparting training as per the provisions laid down under Rule 157 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, including the training modules, the minimum numbers of theory sessions, practical/demonstrations and on-the-job training with their duration, assessment of training needs, post-training evaluation, certification, record- keeping and auditing of records.
1.2 The scheme shall be in consistence with the provisions of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026 and orders issued thereunder, including establishment of training centre, provision of staff, equipment and others facilities of training centre, and appointment of training officer, instructors and trainers.
1.3 Except where othemise exempted under Rule 160 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, all training under the training scheme shall be during normal working hours on full day release system.
1.4 Special Training-The training scheme shall provide for Special Training required under Rule 161, of duration not less than three days.
1.5 Training after long absence or accident or change of job-The training scheme shall provide for training after long absence or accident or change of job required under Rule 162, of duration not less than three days.
1.6 Other Training -The training scheme may include for providing any need-based training in addition to that specified under para 2.1 to 2.3, as may be required or deemed necessary by the employer. The duration of such training shall be decided by the employer based on the objective and purpose of the training.

3.6 CATEGORY Vl- 3.6.1 Special Training (under rule 161)
Prior to the introduction of any New Technology, Equipment and system of work, all concerned persons for operation maintenance and supervision shall be imparted special training of not less than 03 days consisting of theory classes, practical demonstrations and field visits as may be required. Technical representatives of equipment manufacturers, suppliers and other domain experts shall also be engaged in imparting such trainings.
3.6.2 Training after long absence or after an accident or change of job ( Rule 162)
(i) Training after long absence Whenever a person returns to employment in a mine after an absence from work for a period exceeding one year, before re-employment he shall be imparted training of not less than 03 days consisting of minimum six (6) modules or sessions of classroom training and three(3) visits/demonstrations (practical , covering — i. Subjects under General Safety and Trade/Discipline/ Category specific topics as mentioned in Part II &III of Initial training ii. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Code of Practices (COPs), Standing Orders, Standards, Protocols, etc. relevant to his/her nature of job.
iii. First aid, firefighting and other emergency including mock rehearsals.
(ii) Training after an accident Whenever a person returns to work after being involved in a serious accident or in a dangerous occurrence which could have resulted in threat to life and safety in a mine, before re-employment he/she shall be imparted training of not less than 03 days consisting of minimum six (6) modules or sessions of classroom training and three (3) visits/demonstrations /practical, covering — i. Subjects under General Safety and Trade/Discipline/ Category specific topics as mentioned in Part II &III of Initial training ii. Learnings from the accident or dangerous occurrence and other similar accidents, dangerous occurrences and near-misses.
iii. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Code of Practices (COPs), Standing Orders, Standards, Protocols, etc. relevant to his/her nature of job.
iv. First aid, firefighting and other emergency including mock rehearsals.
(iii) Training after change of job Whenever a person is employed on a job which is different from what such person had been performing earlier before such reemployment he/she shall be imparted training of not less than 03 days consisting of minimum six (6) modules or sessions of classroom training and three (3)
visits/demonstrations /practical, covering — i. Subjects under General Safety and Trade/Discipline/ Category specific topics as mentioned in Part II &III of Initial training ii. Specific details of new work, new job-related code of practices, and other applicable safety aspects.
iii. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Code of Practices (COPs), Standing Orders, Standards, Protocols, etc. relevant to his/her nature of job.
iv. First aid, firefighting and other emergency including mock rehearsals.
3.6.3 Other Training The contents of modules of any need-based training other than that specified in para 3.1 to 3.5, 3.6.1 and 3.6.2 shall be decided by the employer based on objective and purpose of the training.
4.0 ASSESSMENT:
The training scheme shall provide for:
i. Assessment of the existing competency, experience and prior learning of persons employed or proposed to be employed in the mine for determining their individual training needs, as required under Rule ii. Identification and periodic assessment of the training needs of persons employed in the mine having regard to the requirements for safe performance of mining operations and prevention of accidents and occupational risks, as required under Rule 157(3) (v).
5.0 MAINTENANCE, RETENTION AND AUDITING OF RECORDS:
The training scheme shall provide for:
i. Maintenance of digital and physical records of all assessments, attendance registers, training logs, evaluation scores, training certificates issued, appointments of training officer, instructors and trainers and any other record at the Vocational Training Centre and at the Mine Manager's office.
ii. Retention of the records for the entire duration of the employee's service and for a minimum of five (5) years thereafter.
iii. A system of periodic auditing of records related to training and assessment at a training center.
6.0 REVIEW OF THE SCHEME The Scheme of Training shall be reviewed at least once every five years, or earlier whenever considered necessary, having regard to changes in technology, mining methods, accident experience, emerging risks, statutory requirements and directions issued by the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator.
7.0 COMPLIANCE The employer and training officer shall ensure effective implementation of the Training Scheme, training records, competency assessment records and audit reports for inspection by the Inspector-cum- Facilitator or any other competent authority whenever required.
8.0 Nothing contained in these guidelines shall be construed as relieving the employer, manager or any other person of any obligation imposed under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, the rules made thereunder, or any other applicable law for the time being in force.
Ujjwal Tah, Director General of Mines Safety & Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator of Mines

title: Testing standards for permitted e-Exploders in underground mines
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular (Approval) 07 of 2026 — Testing standards for permitted e-Exploders in underground mines
text:
of India of Labour & Employment General of Mines safety BRIC 02026 No. DGMS(Tech.)/ S&T/CircuIar (Approval) No. Dhanbad, dated To All Mine Owners, Agents and Managers;
All Manufacturers of e-Exploders & e-Detonators;
All scientific and other institutions related to testing of e-Exploders & e-Detonators.
Subject: Guidelines for Testing Standards of permitted e-ExpIoder for use in underground mines.
Sir,
1. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) had issued Gazette Notification No. S.O. 4255(E) dated 29th September 2023, regarding the phased discontinuation of electric detonators concerning the issues of public safety and National security. The government's assessment concluded the need for complete prohibition of electric detonator by the end of FY 2024-25.
2. As a result, the blasting technology in the mining industry depended on the new development i.e. Electronic Detonator (e-Detonator) and Electronic Exploder (e- Exploder) system. As there was no guidelines/standards for construction, testing and use of e-Exploder. This resulted into the situation that no approved e-Exploder was available to fire the e-Detonators in underground coal mines which may stop the coal production from underground mines. Although, standards for e-detonator were developed and notified as IS 18462:2023, however few manufacturers developed the products [e-Detonator & e-Exploder].
3. Keeping in view of this situation, the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS)
constituted a committee to prepare Guidelines for e-Exploder, particularly to be used in coal mines and underground metalliferous mines (gassy, where Regulation 142 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 is applicable) and other hazardous locations. The Committee consisted of members from the DGMS, CSIR-CIMFR, IIT- ISM, CIL, CMPDIL and representatives from explosive and accessories manufacturers (M/s SOLAR, M/s CDET, M/s IDEAL, M/s Regenesis Industries Pvt. Ltd. and M/s Kakatiya Industries).
4. The detailed deliberations were made by the committee in physical and Hybrid mode.
The draft e-Exploder Guidelines were finally prepared and circulated to all concerned on 16thJuly, 2024. On the basis of these guidelines, around 5 manufacturers (Solar, 125qtqf 125th year in the service to the Nation C-Det, IDEAL, Regenesis and Kakatiya) manufactured the e-Exploders which were tested at CISR-CIMFR, Dhanbad and other Govt./NABL approved Labs.
5. In this regard, deliberations were also made in the National Workshop on "Latest Advancements in the Use of Explosives and Blasting Technology in Mines and the Way Forward" conducted at Ranchi on 14th & 15th November, 2025, in which approximately 250 participants, including manufacturers, scientists, academicians, product experts, and industry users, took part. Inputs of this workshop were also addressed in the guidelines.
6. Further, a meeting was convened on 06.04.2026 at the DGMS Headquarters, attended by representatives of equipment manufacturers, accredited test houses, academicians, scientists, and officials of DGMS. The meeting reviewed the testing protocol of the e- Exploder prepared by the Committee.
7. After detailed discussion and deliberations on the various aspect of test standards and passing out criteria of e-Exploders for use in underground coal mines and underground metalliferous mines (gassy, where Regulation 142 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 is applicable), a set of guidelines were framed which is given at Annexure-I (Appendix-A, Appendix-B & Appendix-C).
8. In this connection, Department of Consumer Affairs, Bureau of Indian Standards has also issued "IS 19359: 2026 e-Exploders-Specification" regarding the testing standards required to be done for e-Exploder before approval and before placing them into use in mines, vide Gazette notification Ref: HQ-PUB013/1/2020-PUB-BIS (1546) New Delhi, the 27th May, 2026, enclosed as Annexure-II.
9. All user(s), manufacturers of e-Exploders and all scientific and other institutions related to testing of e-Exploders & e-Detonators should ensure through a mechanism established for the purpose that e-Exploders have complied with the relevant standards and guidelines before putting them into use in coal mines and underground metalliferous mines (gassy, where Regulation 142 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 is applicable).
IO. All user(s) in consultation with respective manufacturers shall prepare a comprehensive SOP for storage, transport, handling, charging and firing of e- Detonator with e- Exploder (Electronic blasting system) and the same shall be strictly complied with.
-4JJWaI Tah)
Director General of Mines Safety/ Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator of Mines 125qt 125th year in the service to the Nation Annexure — I e-ExpIoder — (Guidelines)
FOREWORD An Electronic Exploder (e-Exploder) is a set of devices consisting of a Logger, a Blaster and a Continuity Tester as independent devices with distinct functions and with independent authorization to ensure safe use.
This device(s) may be used exclusively to communicate with electronic detonators. They usually come with a specific method and protocol of communication compatible to a specific electronic detonator built with the same method and protocol of communication structure and so shall not be interchangeable. In Electronic Detonator systems, an e-ExpIoder from one manufacturer shall not initiate Electronic Detonators from another manufacturer due to differing communication systems bemteen the e-Exploder and Electronic Detonators.
The e-Exploder comes in a form easy to carry to the mine Ifield by an authorized shotfirer and contains a human interface option in the form of a key-board or other form with multiple operational options that can be used to issue different operational commands to complete the process of defining, programming, checking and finally firing of each batch of electronic detonators. e- Exploders come with construction features suitable to be used both in underground mines and in open cast mines.
The e-exploder shall facilitate operation of the blasting from a safe distance and e-Exploder meant for use in underground mines shall additionally come with intrinsically safe features as approved by Director General Mines Safety (DGMS).
The e-Exploder comes with core features to check the health status of the electronic detonator at preliminary stage, to load the serial number and delay time in each electronic detonator at next stage and to check and confirm the electrical connectivity of each detonator to the trunk line cable prior to the blasting phase; once moved to the blasting phase, the e-Exploder shall offer features like checking the attendance of all connected electronic detonators, to initiate charge loading and a possible verification of the same and then after moving to issue the final fire command with a provision for issuing a defuse/abort command to meet some uncommon eventualities.
The e-Exploder comes in a packing case easy to carry and robust enough to withstand the rigors in a mine environment and also equipped with a physical access key to turn on and turn off in addition to a password-based authentication for issue of commands.
1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements of e-Exploders and portable blasting/logging instruments used for shot firing operations for activating electronic detonator(s) during mining and non-mining blasting operations.
2. DEFINITIONS:
2.1 Electronic detonator: Detonator assembly in which the time delay is achieved by means of an electronic chip activated by electronic signature signal/ stimuli.
2.2 Electronic Exploder System [e-ExpIoderl.• A set of devices which uses electrical energy and coded signal for programming/communicating/verifying/activating/initiating/ blasting of electronic detonator(s). It consists of a Logger, a Blaster and a Continuity Tester as independent devices with distinct functions and with independent authorization to ensure safe use.
125qfif 125th year in the service to the Nation 2.3 Programmer: Also called as logger is an instrument used to program the serial number and the required delay into an electronic detonator with a mechanism to verify the same along with the healthiness of the detonator(s).
2.4 Blaster: Blaster is an instrument used to carry out the final operations in the blasting sequence involving verification of the connected detonators from the firing chamber, to arm or charge the detonators and to issue the fire/defuse command.
2.5 The continuity tester: Also known as connection tester is an instrument to verify the parallel connection of each detonator to the trunk line. The continuity tester used in underground mines will additionally come with intrinsically safe features as approved by Director General Mines safety (DGMS).
3. CLASSIFICATIONS:
3.1 The e-Exploders covered by this standard shall be either of the following two types:
Permitted Type -A type which is approved by the statutory authority namely, Directorate General of Mines Safety, for use in underground coal mines, underground Metalliferous mines (gassy, where Regulation 142 of the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 is applicable) and other hazardous locations.
General or Non-permitted Type - A type which is used for mining operations in open places or civil work where the danger from flammable gases is not present.
4.0 CONSTRUCTION AND GENERAL REQUIREMENTS:
4.1 The e-Exploder shall be so constructed that all parts are of satisfactory strength for the service intended. The enclosure case shall be robust such that it meets the requirements of Clause No. 8.4 and 8.5, splash proof and dust tight (degree of protection IP 54) in accordance with IS/IEC 60529:2001* as amended time to time.
The enclosure of the permitted type e-Exploders shall be so constructed as not to give rise to ignition hazard of gas and coal dust due to frictional spark, static charges and leakage current.
The circuit of the e-Exploder shall be intrinsically safe conforming to IEC/IS: 60079-11-2023#, as amended time to time.
( *Specification for degrees of protection provided by enclosures for Iow-voltage switchgear and control gear.)
[ # Explosive Atmospheres: Equipment Protection by Intrinsic Safety "ia'l 4.2 Carrying Strap/handle/Case- A carrying strap/handle shall be fastened securely to the body of the e-Exploder or its carrying case. The carrying strap shall be of adequate strength to withstand an additional 50 percent weight of e-Exploder for 15 miqutes without failure or break.
4.3 The output terminals shall be provided with suitable connecting devices for firm connections.
It should not be possible to remove the connecting device from its position. It shall be possible for easy and firm connection of shot firing cable with the terminals.
4.4 The firing circuit of the e-Exploder shall be adequately insulated from its enclosure and shall meet the requirements given in Clause No. 8.1.
4.5 It shall not be possible to keep the e-Exploder devices in "ON" condition unless the key is 12fi 125th year in the service to the Nation •inserted. The operating key shall be specific to each e-Exploder to avoid the operations by unauthorized persons using a generally available key of similar design or construction.
4.6 The e-Exploder (Blasting unit) shall be so constructed that:
a) It shall be operated by a removable key followed by an authentication password for activation.
b) The arming/fire command from the blaster of the e-Exploder shall be by an additional and separate password enabled operation.
c) No residual energy is left at the terminals after the completion of operation sequence.
d) The circuit of the blasting unit shall be intrinsically safe conforming to IEC/IS: 60079-11-2023, as amended time to time.
4.7 The permitted type e-Exploders shall have suitable devices to terminate the output energy pulse within four milliseconds of the release of the firing command.
4.8 Each e-Exploder shall be capable of firing a prescribed number of electronic detonators in the manner recommended by the manufacturer of the e-Exploder. The performance requirements of the e-Exploder shall be in accordance with Clause No. 6.0.
4.9 In the case of a battery-operated e-Exploders, it shall be possible to either charge or replace the battery without disturbing or damaging components or circuit connections and without allowing the internal temperature to raise beyond 60 degrees centigrade. Replacement or charging of battery shall not be done belowground.
4.10 The e-Exploder shall provide suitable display and shall have an inbuilt feature such that the output terminals will become live only when the battery charge level is sufficient to complete the planned firing operation. There shall be visible indication of the battery charge level and shall have a built-in feature of auto shut off in the event the battery is unable to complete the firing operation unless charged.
4.11 The permitted type of e-Exploder shall also meet the following requirements:
Batch Testing of e-Exploder: Prior to use in mines, the manufacturer shall ensure that the exploder are subjected to the batch testing which shall include test of peak open circuit voltage across output terminals of the e-Exploder, residual charge which should be zero and duration of current impulse to the line which should be within four milliseconds of the operation of the firing command/switch. The manufacturer and users shall ensure that the samples of e-Exploders are drawn on random basis and consignment of the samples sealed jointly by the manufacturer and users. The number of samples to be drawn shall be@ of 1% of the total number of the procured exploders or a minimum of one e-exploder whichever is more and tested at Government approved laboratories / test houses accredited by NABL [subject to confirmation of its accreditation granted by NABL for the relevant standard and that test house is not a part of any manufacturer's testing facility]. The test house, upon receipt of the sealed sample(s) shall perform the requisite tests mentioned above and send original copies of the test reports both to manufacturer and the users which shall be maintained by them. In case, any of the samples fails in the above tests, the whole batch shall be discarded and no e-exploder shall be put into use.
4.12 Electrical Connections: All internal electrical connections shall be mechanically secured or soldered or brazed such that the e-Exploder meets the requirements of drop test and impact test (see Clause No. 8.4 and 8.5).

8.1 Insulation Resistance Test - The e-Exploder shall be kept for 24 hours in the humidity cabinet maintained at 27 +/- 20C and relative humidity not less than 95 percent. The insulation resistance of the exploder after humidity treatment shall be measured by insulation tester with a DC voltage of approximately 500 volts, applied between the line parts and the metal enclosure. The measurement shall be made one minute after the application of voltage. The insulation resistance so measured shall be not less than 50 mega ohm.

C-1 INTRODUCTION The e-Exploder conducts a series of operations before the detonators are blasted. Where in there can be scenarios, which require the blast sequences to be aborted in between. Thus, e-Exploder must have a built-in safe abort mechanism.
An e-Exploder unit must have a switch/button which can override all the on-going sequences and revert detonators to a safe state while also disabling the Firing functionality. The manufacturer shall also declare the time required (after aborting and bus line disconnection) when the detonators can be considered safe.
C-2 PROCEDURE Below test shall be conducted with the maximum no. of detonator supported by the e- Exploder declared by the manufacturer.
1. Connect the detonators with the blaster.
2. Start blast Sequence and bring the samples to charged or armed state, where they can initiate on receiving the firing signal.
3. Wait for 1 minute to ensure that the detonators will not explode in the absence of the firing command.
4. Issue 'Abort' command after which the detonators shall disarm/discharge in the time specified by the manufacturer or within 30 seconds whichever is less and shall revert to disarm/defuse state.
[Manufacturer shall provide the procedure to verify that the left-over stored energy will be less than the no fire energy of the fuse head in the e-detonator].

f) Whether there was any loss of connectivity in attendance check
g) Whether there was any failure in charging up
h) The results shall indicate that whether all the connected detonators have defused/disarmed.

An electronic exploder (e-exploder) is a set of devices consisting ofa logger, a blaster and a continuity tester as independent devices with distinct functions and with independent authorization to ensure safe use.
These devices shall be used exclusively for communication with electronic detonators. It shall operate using a specific communication method and protocol compatible only with a corresponding type or model of electronic detonator designed using the same system architecture. Accordingly, e-exploders and electronic detonators from different manufacturers shall not be considered interchangeable. An e-exploder supplied by one manufacturer shall not be capable of initiating electronic detonators supplied by another manufacturer, due to differences in communication systems.
The e-exploder shall be designed to be portable and suitable for handling by an authorized shotfirer for field or mine use. It shall be provided with a human—machine interface, such as a keyboard or other suitable input device, capable of supporting multiple operational functions. These functions shall include, but not be limited to, defining, programming, checking, and initiating firing sequences for a batch of electronic detonators. The construction of the e-exploder shall be suitable for application in both underground and open-cast mining environments.
The e-exploder shall enable operation of the blasting process from a safe distance. For use in underground mines, the e-exploder shall additionally be equipped with intrinsically safe features, duly approved by the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS), Government of India.
The e-exploder shall incorporate essential functionalities to support various operational stages, including:
a) Verification of the health status ofelectronic detonators at the preliminary stage;
b) Loading of serial numbers and delay timings into individual detonators in the programming stage; and
c) Verification and confirmation of electrical connectivity of each electronic detonator to the trunk line cable prior to blasting.
During the blasting phase, the e-exploder shall support the following operations:
a) Checking the attendance ofall connected detonators;
b) Initiating charge loading, with optional verification;
c) Issuing the final fire command; and
d) Providing the capability to issue a defuse or abort command to address unforeseen circumstances.
The e-exploder shall be housed in a robust and portable case designed to endure the mechanical and environmental stresses encountered in mining conditions. It shall be equipped with a physical access control key switching the device on and off, along with password-based authentication tor execution ot-conunands.

title: Procurement of spares for DGMS-approved mining equipment
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 08 of 2026 — Procurement of spares for DGMS-approved mining equipment
text:
Government of India Ministry of Labour & Employment Directorate General of Mines safety DGMS (Tech) No. 08 To, Owners/Agents/Managers of all mines Dhanbad, dated:
Subject: Procurement of spares for Mining Equipment approved by DGMS to Maintain Safety and Functional Integrity.
1.0 Introduction Equipment used in mines, particularly in hazardous and critical applications, are approved by this Directorate considering their design, construction, and safety features in accordance with relevant standards and statutory provisions. Such approvals are granted considering the equipment as a complete system, including its components, sub-assemblies, and safety-critical parts, under Regulation 208(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017, which stipulates:
"All apparatus and appliances shall be maintained in a safe working condition and in accordance with the conditions of approval." 2.0 Observations During inspections, audits, and incident analyses, it has been observed that in certain cases, spares and components other than those supplied by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)/Original Part Manufacturer (OPM) or its authorised dealers are being used in equipment, thereby compromising their safety and functional integrity.
Further, numerous complaints have been received from manufacturers regarding the use of non-OEM/non-OPM and unauthorised spares in their approved equipment. It has also been observed that critical components are being replaced with non-OEM/non-OPM or incompatible substitutes. Such practices may lead to:
i) Reduction in Mechanical strength and load-bearing capacity
ii) Failure of braking and safety systems
iii) Improper functioning of hydraulic and transmission systems
iv) Excessive wear, misalignment, and vibration
v) Failure of interlocks and safety devices In the event of failure of such components, faults may remain undetected or result in catastrophic breakdown. This poses a serious threat to human safety, particularly in underground and opencast mines where heavy machinery operates under demanding conditions.
3.0 Safety Implication Equipment safety relies on the integrity of design, material strength, and compatibility of components. Use of non-genuine or unauthorised spares, especially in safety-critical parts, ot defeats the basis of approval and may render the equipment unsafe for operation. Failure of mechanical systems may result in:
i) Sudden equipment failure or collapse
ii) Runaway or uncontrolled movement
iii) Failure of braking or holding systems
iv) Falling of loads or structural components
v) Increased risk of injury, fatal accidents, and damage to property 4.0 Procurement of Spares: For all equipment approved by this Directorate, the following conditions are incorporated for strict compliance by the user:
4.1 The procurement of the DGMS-approved equipment/spares shall be done from DGMS approved manufacturers or their authorized dealers for all Underground equipment subject to strict adherence of the following conditions:
(i) The equipment/material shall possess valid DGMS approvals and shall conform to the specifications and conditions stipulated therein.
(ii) Authenticity of the approval and supply source shall be verified and relevant documents such as approval letters, test certificates, and authorization from the manufacturer shall be obtained and maintained.
4.2 The procurement of items covered under relevant DGMS general order shall, subject to compliance with the provisions stipulated in the respective in order and all such items shall conform to the technical specifications and safety requirements prescribed under the applicable DGMS general order/relevant BIS/internationally accepted standards and certification.
4.3 The procurement of other components/consumables for which no specific DGMS circular is issued shall be done as per the existing practice of company, however it meets with the relevant BIS standard or any other applicable standards in this regard. The materials and components shall be suitable for the intended Opencast/Underground application and operating conditions. Also, the overall system safety shall not be compromised, and integration of such components shall be compatible with the system in operation.
The responsibility for ensuring safety, suitability, and compliance with statutory provisions of the procured items, materials, devices, or equipment rests with the mine management, i.e.
Owner, Agent, and Manager of the mine. The above requirement shall apply in Underground (UG) mines and Opencast (OC) mines in the interest of safety.
All Owners, Agents, and Managers of mines shall ensure strict compliance with the above rd installations and ensure safety of persons.

title: Carbon Phase Transition Rock Breaking Technique (CPTBT) in opencast mines
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 09 of 2026 — Carbon Phase Transition Rock Breaking Technique (CPTBT) in opencast mines
text:
of India Ministry of Labour & Employment Directorate General of Mines Safety DGMS (Tech) Circular No. /S /2026/ oq Dhanbad, Date 0 8 • To, All Owners, Agent and Managers of Coal and Metalliferous opencast mines BRIC Subject: Fracturing of strata/ground by using Carbon Phase Transition Rock Breaking Technique (CPTBT) in opencast mines — reg.
Carbon Phase Transition Rock Breaking Technique (CPTBT), also known as a carbon dioxide-based blast-free rock-breaking technique, has been experimentally studied for fracturing of strata/ground in one Indian mine. The results of the trials conducted so far have been found to be encouraging and indicate the potential suitability of the technique for controlled rock-fracturing applications in mines.
Since the technique does not involve the detonation of conventional explosives, the generation of induced ground vibration is substantially reduced, thereby minimizing the potential adverse effects of vibration on nearby structures, mine infrastructure, equipment and other installations, subject to the prevailing geological and site-specific conditions.
The technique utilises the rapid phase transition and expansion of liquid carbon dioxide (LC02)
into gaseous C02 within a specially designed high-pressure tube/cylinder placed in a borehole, thereby generating pressure sufficient to fracture the surrounding rock mass without the use of conventional explosives so the risk of uncontrolled projection of rock fragments (fly rock) is substantially reduced in comparison with conventional blasting.
The technique has potential advantages in situations where conventional blasting is undesirable or may pose additional risks. In particular, its use can substantially reduce dependence on explosives for suitable rock-fracturing operations and may be advantageous at locations where structures or other sensitive installations are situated within the danger zone of blasting. The ground vibration associated with CPTBT is expected to be comparatively lower than that associated with conventional explosive blasting, subject to site-specific conditions and the design of the operation.
CPTBT may also be experimented for use in mines or areas having hot strata or other conditions where the use of explosives may pose a risk of premature initiation. As the technique does not involve the use of conventional explosive charges, its adoption may eliminate the risks specifically associated with the storage, transportation, handling and charging of explosives for such rock-fracturing operations, subject to compliance with all applicable statutory safety requirements and conditions prescribed by the competent authority.
The experimental observations further indicate that CPTBT can provide satisfactory rock fragmentation and may be used in conjunction with a suitable rock breaker for achieving the desired degree of fragmentation and secondary size reduction.
In view of the above, and with a view to promoting the adoption of safer and suitable alternative rock- fracturing technologies, the following technical guidelines shall be followed by mine management while adopting CPTBT in opencast mines.
5.
5.1 5.2 5.3 5.4 5.5
1. Scope These guidelines shall apply to the use of Carbon Phase Transition Rock Breaking Technique (CPTBT)
for fracturing of strata/ground in opencast coal and metalliferous mines, subject to compliance with all applicable statutory provisions.
The technique shall be adopted in any mine only after establishing, through a site-specific scientific assessment, the suitability of the ground conditions and the design parameters to be followed for its application, based on an appropriate scientific study, and obtaining prior No objection from Chief Inspector cum Facilitator of mines confirming to the su itability of the proposed application and adequacy of the control measures for managing the hazards associated with high-pressure C02 systems.
2. Risk Assessment and SOP 2.1 A detailed site-specific risk assessment shall be carried out before adoption of CPTBT, covering, inter alia: high-pressure C02 release: failure of rupture disc/activation system; non-initiation or incomplete discharge ofa charged tube: projectile hazards; C02 accumulation and asphyxiation; cold burns/frostbite;
instability of fractured rock/strata; handling and transportation of charged tubes; electrical/ignition hazards.
2.2 Based on the risk assessment and manufacturer's guidelines, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
shall be prepared, by the Mine Manager and implelnented at workplace.
2.3 The SOP shall specifically provide for the safe handling, isolation, recovery and/or controlled depressurisation of C02-filled tubes in the event that the tube fails to discharge or the borehole plug/vent arrangement fails to function as intended.
3. Supervision and Competency 3.1 Fracturing of strata/ground by CPTBT shall be carried out under the direct supervision ofa person holding at least a Manager's Certificate of Competency.
3.2 Only specially trained and authorised work-persons shall be permitted to handle, transport, charge, place and otherwise deal with high-pressure C02-f111ed tubes.
3.3 A competent person, specifically trained in the handling, transportation, charging and initiation of the high-pressure C02-filled tubes, shall be authorised to carry out initiation using the approved initiation system.
4. Design and Preparation of Boreholes 4.1 The borehole diameter, depth, burden, spacing, number of holes, number of rows and other site- specific parameters for CPTBT shall be based on the findings of the scientific/e,xperimental study conducted at the mine or other duly established technical study applicable to the particular geological and mining conditions.
4.2 The area proposed för CPTBT shall be clearly demarcated on the mine surface plan and correspondingly marked in the field.
4.3 Adequate stemming shall be provided to control the ejection of fractured material and premature ejection of the C02 steel tubes from the holes. Measures shall be taken to ensure that fractured projectiles do not travel beyond the prescribed safe limit of IO m from the point of fracture initiation.
Inspection of C02 Tubes and Equipment Every C02-filled steel tube/cylinder and associated component shall be inspected before use.
Tubes having dents, cracks, corrosion, deformation, damaged threads, leaking valves, defective safety devices or expired test certification shall not be used.
Each tube shall have a unique identification number and the relevant information regarding filling, quantity of C02, date of filling, prescribed service life and number/frequency of use shall be recorded.
Filling of the tubes shall be carried out only at an approved/designated filling station using suitable equipment and under controlled conditions. The filled quantity shall conform to the manufacturees specifications.
A standard protocol shall be established and implemented for the examination and inspection ofall C02- filling steel tubes including its components after their use in each round of strata/ground fracture in the mine to ensure free from any physical defects. Non-destructive testing (NDT) of all C02-fllling steel tubes used for fracturing strata/ground shall be conducted periodically as per original manufacturer recommendations.
5.6 5.7 A procedure and guidelines for the identification, isolation and safe disposal/discarding of defective or unserviceable C02-filling steel tubes shall also be formulated in consultation with the original manufacturer and a competent scientific/testing agency and shall be strictly followed.
The heating element shall be stored properly and shall be prevented from any fire hazards.
6. Personal Protective Equipment Persons engaged in handling, transportation, charging and initiation shall be provided with and shall use appropriate PPE. The PPE shall be selected considering the hazards of sudden high-pressure release, projectile generation, extreme cold and C02 exposure.
7. Handling and Transportation 7.1 C02 tubes shall not be dropped, dragged, rolled or subjected to impact or excessive vibration.
7.2 Suitable tube carriers, lifting cradles, cylinder trolleys or other approved handling arrangements shall be used.
7.3 Tubes shall not be lifted by the valve assembly, heating cable or neck fittings.
7.4 During transportation, tubes shall be securely fastened in an upright position, with protective caps/valve guards fitted, and shall be carried in a well-ventilated or open-body vehicle.
7.5 Charged tubes shall not be transported in passenger cabins and shall be protected from direct heat, sunlight, impact and other sources capable of increasing the internal pressure.
7.6 Suitable warning signage indicating the presence of pressurised C02 tubes shall be displayed on the vehicle used for transportation.
8. Charging and Placement 8.1 Charging of liquid C02 shall be carried out only by trained and authorised persons at the designated filling facility.
8.2 Leak detection shall be carried out using an approved method, such as a soapy-water test, and open flame shall not be used for leak detection.
8.3 The charged tube shall be inserted gently into the designated borehole and positioned in accordance with the approved design.
8.4 The area shall be barricaded and access controlled before initiation.
9. Danger Zone and Initiation Before initiation of charged C02 tubes, the competent person/authorised Foreman and Assistant Manager shall ensure that all persons within a radius of 500 metres have taken proper shelter and that the applicable provisions relating to blasting/danger zone are complied with.
9.2 A warning siren or other effective warning signal shall be given before initiation.
9.3 Initiation shall be carried out only from a safe and protected location using a suitable initiation apparatus of a type that does not pose any danger and is certified by the manufacturer in accordance with the standards laid down by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) or relevant international standards.
10. C02 Monitoring and Re-entry 10.1 Since C02 is heavier than air and may accumulate in low-lying or poorly ventilated locations, appropriate precautions shall be taken against C02 accumulation.
10.2 Calibrated C02 and 02 detectors shall be provided to check the accumulation of C02.
10.3 No person shall be allowed to re-enter the place where the rock breaking operations have been done with LC02 unless the C02 is cleared and unless a period ofat least 20 minutes has elapsed from the time of initiation.
11. Non-lnitiation/Misfire of C02 Tube 1 1.1 A charged but non-initiated C02 tube shall be treated as a high-pressure vessel/hazard until it is conclusively established that the pressure has been safely released.
1 1.2 No person shall attempt to drill, cut, hea , hammer, manually vent or otherwise interfere with a suspected non-initiated tube.
I I .3 The area shall remain barricaded and access shall be restricted.
1 1.4 The manufacturer-prescribed waiting period and written mine SOP for safe approach, isolation, depressurisation and recovery shall be strictly followed.
I I .5 Only trained and authorised personnel shall be permitted to deal with such tubes. The source SOP specifically requires non-initiated tubes to be treated as pressurised vessels until safe depressurisation/discharge is confirmed.
I I .6 Where safe recovery is not possible. the borehole may be dealt with in accordance with an approved procedure, after confirmation of pressure decay and with appropriate measures to prevent future interaction with the location.
12. Electrical and Static-Electricity Precautions
12. I Metallic C02 transfer lines. manifolds, cylinder racks and firing panels shall be suitably bonded and earthed.
12.2 Where non-metallic sections are unavoidable, conductive or static-dissipative hoses shall be used and suitably bonded.
12.3 The integrity of the earthing system shall be checked before commencement of CPTBT operations and the relevant readings/checks shall be recorded.
12.4 CPTBT charging and initiation shall not be undertaken where a flammable atmosphere or explosive dust cloud is present in the vicinity of manifolds or borehole collars.
13. Documentation and Record Keeping 13.1 A record of every CPTBT operation shall be maintained in a bound paged book or in a retrievable, non-editable electronic record.
13.2 A record of each round of fracturing of strata/ground, showing the pattern of shot holes and the particulars of spacing & burden of holes, hole depth, number of holes initiated in the round, weight of the liquid C02 filled in tube/hole, total weight of the liquid C02 filled in tubes/round, stemming column length (s), initiation pattern(with proper sketches), activation time, percentage of C02 after initiation at place of experiment, percentage of 02 after initiation at place of experiment, results of ground vibrations observed (PPV, frequency & air over pressure), fragmentation, throw, back-break, breakage pattern and distance up to which flying fragments travelled shall be maintained in a bound paged book kept for the purpose and countersigned by the Manager/Agent/Owner of the mine.
13.3 The record shall be maintained by the competent person in charge of the operation and countersigned by the Mine Manager.
14. General
14. I CPTBT shall be adopted only after carrying out a site-specific risk assessment and establishing the suitability of the technique for the geological and mining conditions.
14.2 The manufacturer's technical and safety instructions shall be followed in addition to the requirements contained in this Circular.
14.3 No relaxation from any statutory requirement shall be presumed merely on account of the use of CPTBT instead of conventional explosives.
14.4 The provisions relating to precautions while handling apparatus under pressure shall also be strictly complied with.
14.5 Mine management shall ensure that all persons associated with CPTBT operations are adequately trained, competent and medically fit for the work assigned to them.
All concerned mine managements are therefore advised to ensure strict compliance with the above guidelines w adoptin P TBT for fracturing of strata/ground.
