title: OEM spares in approved electrical equipment, and preserving flameproof and intrinsic safety protection
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 10 of 2026 — OEM spares in approved electrical equipment, and preserving flameproof and intrinsic safety protection
text:
/ Government of India / Ministry of Labour & Employment / Directorate General of Mines safety DGMS (Tech) Circular No. Io To, Owners/Agents/Managers of all mines QR. 06-2-00-6 Dhanbad, dated:
Subject: Use of OEM/OPM/Authorised Spares in DGMS Approved Electrical Equipment for Preservation of Flameproof (FLP) and Intrinsic Safety (IS) Protection Philosophy — Reg.
1.0 Introduction Electrical equipment used in mines, particularly in hazardous areas, is approved by this Directorate with specific methods of protection such as Flameproof (FLP) and Intrinsic Safety (IS) in accordance with the relevant provisions of the IS/IEC 60079 series of standards.
Such approvals are granted after evaluation of the equipment as a complete system, including its components, sub-assemblies, protective circuits, and other safety- critical parts, and are subject to the conditions stipulated under Regulation 208(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017, which provides that:
"A// apparatus and appliances sha// be maintained in a safe working condition and in accordance with the conditions of approval. " 2.0 Observations During inspections and based on complaints received from manufacturers, it has been observed that non-OEM/unauthorised spares and incompatible substitute components are being used in DGMS-approved electrical equipment, including protective and control circuit devices such as relays, current transformers (CTs), interposing relays, contactors, sensors, electronic modules, and associated devices.
Such practices may:
Compromise the flameproof integrity of enclosures;
page Alter intrinsically safe parameters;
Cause malfunction or failure of protective, interlocking, and permissive schemes; and Result in incorrect sensing and operation of protection systems.
Failure of such systems may leave electrical faults undetected or unisolated, leading to overheating, arcing, sparking, or hazardous touch potentials, thereby posing a serious risk of fatality or injury. In underground mines, the presence of methane further increases the risk of ignition of an explosive atmosphere.
3.0 Safety Implications FLP protection depends upon the integrity of the enclosure to contain an internal explosion, while IS protection relies upon maintaining electrical and thermal energy within certified safe limits.
The use of non-genuine or unauthorised spares may alter the certified safety parameters and impair the protection philosophy on the basis of which the approval was granted.
4.0 Compliance Directions In the interest of safety, the following shall be strictly ensured:
4.1 Use of OEM/OPM/Authorised Spares
(i) Only spares, components, and accessories supplied by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Original Part Manufacturer (OPM), or their authorised dealers shall be used in DGMS-approved electrical equipment.
(ii) This requirement shall apply to all safety-critical components, including protective and control circuit devices, flameproof joints and fasteners, cable glands, intrinsically safe interfaces, sensors, and associated electrical and electronic devices.
(iii) No substitution, modification, replacement, or retrofitting shall be carried out unless the replacement component is identical in specification and safety characteristics to the approved component.
(iv) Any replacement or alteration that affects, or is likely to affect, the Flameproof (FLP) enclosure integrity, Intrinsic Safety (IS) parameters, energy-limiting characteristics, creepage and clearance distances, ingress protection, thermal characteristics, fault-withstand capability, or the certified protection philosophy of the equipment shall constitute a material deviation from the approved design and shall be deemed to impair the safety characteristics on the basis of which the approval was granted, thereby posing a risk to the safety of persons employed in the mine.
pct9e 0'1.0+02 4.2 Maintenance and Repair All maintenance, repair, overhaul, refurbishment, and rebuilding activities shall be carried out exclusively using OEM/OPM or authorised spares.
The replacement parts shall be identical to the approved components in all safety- critical respects, including flameproof joint dimensions, material specifications, and the certified ratings and safety parameters of electrical and electronic components such as resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, Zener diodes, integrated circuits (ICs), transformers, semiconductors, and other associated devices, so as not to impair the FLP or IS protection philosophy.
5.0 Enforcement All Owners, Agents, Managers, manufacturers, repairers, rebuilders, suppliers, and users of approved electrical equipment shall ensure strict compliance with these directions to safeguard electrical installations and the safety of persons employed in mines.

title: Rock mass classification and support/slope design in metalliferous mines
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 11 of 2026 — Rock mass classification and support/slope design in metalliferous mines
text:
/ Government of India /Ministry of Labour & Employment /Directorate General of Mines safety BRIC DGMS Circular No.1Eof 2026 To Dhanbad, dated ag/ 08 / 2026 All the Owners, Agents and Managers of Metalliferous Mines Subject: Guidelines for use of Rock Mass Classifications and Support/Slope Design for Improving Stability of Workings in Metalliferous Mines.
Sir, Stability of workings is essential for economic and safe exploitation of mineral from mines. The geotechnical assessment, safe support/slope design and monitoring of stability of workings is one of the major challenges in Indian Metalliferous Mines. The stability analysis of mine workings, support/slope design and their monitoring is not yet an integral part of mine planning. In Indian mining conditions, support/slope design guidelines are yet to be formulated for different types of mining practices for maintaining safety and productivity.
However, there is a lot of diversity amongst different mines in understanding and practicing for Rock Mass Classification systems and Support/Slope Designs. Therefore, it was felt necessary to evolve a broad standardization/ guideline for use of Rock Mass Classifications and Support/Slope Design for Improving Stability of Workings in Metalliferous Mines.
In view of the above, a workshop on the subject "Rock Mass Classifications and Support Design for Improving Stability of Workings in Metal Mines" was jointly organised by DGMS and IIT Kharagpur on 28th November 2025 in Jaipur, Rajasthan to deliberate and review the present status of use of different types of Rock Mass Classification systems and Support/Slope Designs. In this workshop standard guidelines are finalized for use of Rock Mass Classifications and Support/Slope Design methodologies for Improving Stability of Workings in Metalliferous Mines. This workshop was attended by about 80 officials and experts from regulatory authorities, academic institutions, research organizations, and various mining industries like DGMS, IITs, NITS, NIRM, CIMFR, M/s HZL, M/s HCL,M/s MOIL, M/s UCIL, M/s IMFA, M/s OMC, M/s Birla Corporation Ltd., M/S Jindal Saw Ltd., M/s JK Cement, M/s JSW Cement, M/s Wonder Cement Ltd., M/s Ultratech Cement, M/s Shree Cement Ltd., M/s Mangalam Cement Ltd., M/s Nuvoco Vistas Corporation Limited, M/s RK Marble Limited, M/s Shree Cement Limited, M/s UMDS Pvt. Ltd., etc., in which 10 technical presentations were made by different experts giving valuable inputs on the subject matter.
Based on various inputs drawn from the detailed deliberations and discussions made in the workshop, the following guidelines are being made for use of Rock Mass Classifications and Support/Slope Design for Improving Stability of Workings in Metalliferous Mines.
1. GSI and Q values shall be calculated by practicing geologists and mining engineers at multiple locations and levels based on the complexity of the geology and geotechnical domain within underground mines. Structured training shall be provided to these personnel for the correct application of these systems.
2. It is time for the Indian metal mining sector to adopt Q and GSI as standard systems for rock mass classification and support design. RMR shall gradually be replaced by Q or GSI, particularly in underground mines and shall be incorporated in technical and scientific study reports, A step-by-step support design procedure using the Q system is provided in Appendix A, and the application of GSI in bolt design and numerical modelling is outlined in Appendix B.
3. The NGI support design chart shall be used for determining support requirements in drives, drifts, cross-cuts, and other underground excavations. Installed support systems may initially be benchmarked against NGI recommendations, and if any discrepancies found, it shall be scientifically investigated and rectified.
4. In slope stability analysis, overall slope stability shall be assessed using rock mass properties-such as cohesion and friction angle-adjusted through GSI values measured at different slope locations depending on the complexity of the geology and geotechnical domain. Q-slope method or Slope Mass Rating (SMR) shall be used to estimate rock mass quality and bench slope angles to validate the slope stability analysis. A step-by-step methodology is provided in Appendix C for Q-slope and in Appendix D for SMR.
5. Scientific organisations, academic institutions, and mining companies shall adopt Q- or GSI-based approaches for adjusting rock mass properties to replicate field conditions in numerical models for bringing uniformity in stability assessment and generate data to develop support/slope design charts for site specific conditions.
6. Periodical/ real-time support performance monitoring like load—displacement, pillar stresses and roof displacements is crucial for understanding rock mass behaviour and validating numerical model outcomes. It shall be carried out at various locations near the active stopes, junctions, geologically disturbed areas and a Trigger Action Response Plan (TARP) shall be developed based on numerical and monitoring data.
7. Slope bench movement shall be monitored regularly or in real time to generate heat maps of displacements and validate the slope stability analysis. Zones showing major displacement ("hot zones") shall be identified and TARP shall be developed based on numerical and monitoring data.
8. Mine management shall establish a dedicated Geotechnical Cell, comprising trained geologists and mining engineers with expertise in rock mechanics, ground control, and support/slope design. This team shall be regularly kept updated in the application of GSI, Q, Q-slope and SMR methods, stability analysis of stopes/slopes and monitoring to develop robust mine/support / slope design.
9. In the unorganized sector, small mine owners often lack access to advanced technology, skilled manpower, and proper safety systems. They shall seek technical guidance from nearby mines in the organised sector or any other experts in the concerned field.
All the Owners, Agents and Managers are advised to prepare Strata/Ground Control Management Plan keeping in view of the above-mentioned guidelines.
Ujj I Tah Directorate General of Mines Safety Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator of Mines Enclosure to DGMS (Tech)/S&T/Circular No.

title: Employment of women in mines
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 12 of 2026 — Employment of women in mines
text:
of India of Labour & Employment General of Mines safety Dhanbad, dated:
BRtC No.
To:
The Owner, Agent, Manager of all Mines and manufacturers of mining equipment/ appliances Subject: Employment of Women in Mines The Central Government, in exercise of the powers conferred by the sub-section (2) of section I of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (37 of 2020), appointed the 21st day of November, 2025 as the date on which the provisions of the said Code, have come into force [S.O. 5321(E)]. As per the said Code, the following sections provides the special provisions relating to employment of women in all establishments, including mines:
Section 43. Women shall be entitled to be employed in all establishments for all types of work under this Code and they may also be employed, with their consent before 6 a.m. and beyond 7 p.m. subject to such conditions relating to safety, holidays and working hours or any other condition to be observed by the employer as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government.
Section 44. Where the appropriate Government considers that the employment of women is dangerous for their health and safety, in an establishment or class of establishments or in any particular hazardous or dangerous processes in such establishment or class of establishments, due to the operation carried out therein, such Government may in the prescribed manner, require the employer to provide adequate safeguards prior to the employment of women for such operation.
Subsequently, the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, also came into force under the Code with effect from 8th Mayt 2026, under which Rule 83 on "Employment of women in establishment" and Rule 84 on "Adequate safety of employment of women in dangerous operations" stipulate further provisions on the subject.
In this regard, comprehensive guidelines were also issued earlier vide circular No. DGMS (Legis.)/Circular No.02, dated 24.05.2019 for framing SOPs for adoption by the mine owner/ mine management during employment of women in their respective mines 125Äta€/ 125th year in the serving to the Nation" Page I I of 5 In view of the growing women deployment in underground and opencast mines under various categories of jobs, a conclave on "Women in Mining" was organized on 26.11.2025 by DGMS South Eastern Zone, Ranchi, to review the present status of women employment and to deliberate on the issues related to the women employees deployed in mines. About 206 participants from DGMS, M/s. Tata Steel Ltd., M/s. CIL, M/s. CCL, M/s. SCCL, M/s. NML, M/s.
HZL, etc., including 136 female and 03 diverse gender employees, attended the conclave.
Based on the inputs drawn and suggestions received from the conclave, apart from the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026, the following further guidelines are made:

The heavy earth-moving machinery (HEMM) should be ergonomically designed considering the following aspects for women employees:
a. different human body types and strength levels to ensure ease of operation (lower forces, better visibility) to prevent injuries and improve comfort.
b. adjustable seats and seat belts to fit a wider range of user body sizes (anthropometry), c. a suitable access system with hydraulic operated ladders (wherever required) for ease of riding on to the equipment, d. customizable controls and tool shapes that accommodate a wider range of users, considering factors like shorter limbs, different strength distributions, and grip sizes.
Portable wash room shall be provided at nearby location for HEMM operators (such as shovels) deployed in opencast mines.
The women employed in mines shall be provided with the PPEs, like gum boots, helmets, gloves and reflective jackets, etc., designed to suit/fit them.
Awareness programs for family members shall also be conducted to help them understand the importance of women's employment in such roles, and to resolve the issues related to domestic abuse.
The management of mines employing women shall provide a separate complaint or suggestion box for women employees, and such complaints along with the cases of language or verbal abuse by male employees toward female employees shall be resolved by the Internal Complaints Committee established under the POSH Act.
Information about hazards associated with respective workplaces shall be informed to the women employee. Consent form duly signed by women employee shall be kept maintained clearly specifying the details of the workplace, working hours, and applicable shift timings for the job. Sample consent form as in Annexure-I may be used for record.
No woman shall be deployed during pregnancy in hazardous environments or on arduous work, such as HEMM operations, underground workings, or other similar activities, without the prior consent and medical clearance of the attending doctor and also not be deployed in such hazardous environments or on such arduous work for a period of at least three (3)
months after childbirth.

In case women employees are deployed in below-ground workings of a mine, not less than three (3) women employees shall be deployed at any place at any time.
10. Display at conspicuous spaces in local language, the penal consequences of sexual harassment of women at workplace and the order constituting Internal Complaints under POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) Act, 2013.
11. The Owners, Agents and Managers of all mines and the manufacturers of mining equipment/ appliances are requested to ensure compliance of the above guidelines.

title: Management of spares for DGMS-approved mining equipment
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 13 of 2026 — Management of spares for DGMS-approved mining equipment
text:
of India of Labour & Employment General of Mines safety BRIC DGMS (Tech) (S&T) Circular No. 13 To, Owners/Agents/Managers of all mines Dhanbad, dated: 31) b 8/20 Subject: management of spares for Mining Equipment approved by DGMS to Maintain Safety and Functional Integrity.
1.0 Introduction Equipment used in mines, particularly in hazardous and critical applications, are approved by this Directorate considering their design, construction, and safety features in accordance with relevant standards and statutory provisions. Such approvals are granted considering the equipment as a complete system, including its components, sub-assemblies, and safety-critical parts, under Regulation 208(3) of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017, which stipulates:
"All apparatus and appliances shall be maintained in a safe working condition and in accordance with the conditions of approval." 2.0 Observations During inspections, audits, and incident analyses, it has been observed that in certain cases, spares and components other than those supplied by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)/OriginaI Part Manufacturer (OPM) or its authorised dealers are being used in equipment, thereby compromising their safety and functional integrity.
Further, numerous complaints have been received from manufacturers regarding the use of non-OEM/non- OPM and unauthorised spares in their approved equipment. It has also been observed that critical components are being replaced with non-OEM/non-OPM or incompatible substitutes. Such practices may lead to:
i) Reduction in Mechanical strength and load-bearing capacity
ii) Failure of braking and safety systems
iii) Improper functioning of hydraulic and transmission systems
iv) Excessive wear, misalignment, and vibration
v) Failure of interlocks and safety devices In the event of failure of such components, faults may remain undetected or result in catastrophic breakdown. This poses a serious threat to human safety, particularly in underground and opencast mines where heavy machinery operates under demanding conditions.
Page | 1 of 3 3.0 Safety Implication Equipment safety relies on the integrity of design, material strength, and compatibility of components. Use of non-genuine or unauthorised spares, especially in safety-critical parts, defeats the basis of approval and may render the equipment unsafe for operation. Failure of mechanical systems may result in:
i) Sudden equipment failure or collapse
ii) Runaway or uncontrolled movement
iii) Failure of braking or holding systems
iv) Falling of loads or structural components
v) Increased risk of injury, fatal accidents, and damage to property 4.0 Management of Spares: For all equipment approved by this Directorate, the following conditions are incorporated for strict compliance by the user:
4.1 Equipment, spares and materials requiring approval of the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS)
shall be used only supplied from the manufacturer in whose favour DGMS approval has been granted for that specific item or model, or from a dealer holding a valid written authorisation from such manufacturer for that item, subject to the following conditions:
(i) The item supplied shall be covered by a DGMS approval that is valid and subsisting on the date of supply, and shall conform in every respect to the specifications, terms, conditions and limitations stipulated in that approval.
(ii) At the time of acceptance of supply, the indenting/procuring authority shall verify the genuineness of the DGMS approval and of the supply source. The following documents shall be obtained from the supplier and maintained on record:
(a) copy of the DGMS approval letter together with the approved drawings, specifications and all amendments/extensions thereto;
(b) type-test and routine-test certificates issued by a laboratory recognised for the purpose, conforming to the latest revision of the applicable standard;
(c) in the case of supply through a dealer, the manufacturer's letter of authorisation, valid on the date of supply, expressly covering the item supplied;
(d) the manufacturer's certificate of conformity confirming that the item supplied is identical to the item approved by DGMS.
These records shall be retained for the service life of the equipment or for such period as may be prescribed, whichever is longer, and shall be produced on demand to the Inspecting Officer.
4.2 Items covered under a DGMS General Order shall be used in compliance with all provisions stipulated in the respective General Order, and shall conform to the technical specifications and safety requirements prescribed in the applicable standard determined in the following order of precedence:
(i) the relevant Indian Standard issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS);
(ii) where the Indian Standard is harmonised with the corresponding international standard, the harmonised Indian Standard;
(iii) where no Indian Standard exists for the item, the relevant International Standard (IEC/ISO or other recognised international standard);
(iv) where neither an Indian Standard nor an International Standard exists, the national standard of the country of origin of the item.
Page | 2 of 3 The standard applicable shall be the edition in force on the date of opening of the tender, unless the DGMS General Order specifies otherwise.
4.3 Other components and consumables for which no special approval, General Order or other specific guidelines have been issued by DGMS shall be used only after conformation to the relevant Indian Standard (BIS) or, where none exists, to such other applicable standard. Such items shall be suitable for the intended opencast or underground application and the prevailing operating conditions, shall be compatible with the system into which they are integrated, and shall not compromise the overall safety of that system.
The responsibility for ensuring safety, suitability, and compliance with statutory provisions for used items, materials, devices, or equipment rests with the mine management, i.e. Owner, Agent, and Manager of the mine. The above requirement shall apply in Underground (UG) mines and Opencast (OC) mines in the interest of safety.
This Circular supersedes DGMS (Tech.)(S&T) Circular No. 08, Dhanbad, dated 27.08.2026.
All Owners, Agents, and Managers of mines and advised to ensure strict compliance with the above directions to safeguard installations and ensure safety of persons.
Yours faithfully Jjwa ah)
Director General of Mines Safety & Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator Page | 3 of 3

title: Guidelines for the use of permitted e-Detonators in underground mines
full_title: DGMS (Tech) Circular 14 of 2026 — Guidelines for the use of permitted e-Detonators in underground mines
text:
of India of Labour & Employment Directorate General of Mines Safety BRIC No. S&T/Circular No.14 Dhanbad, To All Mine Owners, Agents and Managers;
dated 2026 Subject: Guidelines for the use of permitted e-Detonator in underground mines.
1.0 1.1 1.2 1.3 2.0 2.1 2.2 BACKGROUND:
The Government has expressed concerns regarding the dangerous nature of electric detonators, particularly in view of the frequent seizure of illicit explosives by security agencies and the associated public safety and national security concerns.
In this regard, the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) had issued Gazette Notification No. S.O. 4255(E)
dated 29th September 2023, regarding the phased discontinuation of electric detonators.
The above measure has resulted in changeover towards the safer technology which pushed the industry to transition towards the heavily trackable electronic alternatives i.e., electronic detonator. Electronic detonator systems incorporate enhanced traceability and security features, including manufacturer-specific software, password-protected access and user authentication mechanisms, thereby reducing the possibility of unauthorized use or initiation.
INTRODUCTION:
Electronic detonators are modern, fully programmable devices capable of two-way communication. Each detonator contains a circuit board that can be programmed to initiate at a precisely defined time within a firing sequence. Electronic detonators are usually programmed individually using a handheld logger or programmer and are initiated through a firing unit (e-Exploder).
The electronic detonator systems can be fitted or broadly classified into two categories: pre-programmed electronic detonators (or fixed-delay detonators) and programmable-delay detonators. In pre-programmed electronic detonators, the delay time is programmed at the factory before dispatch, and the user cannot change it.
These detonators are normally numbered or coded in such a way that the user can identify their intended delay time. In programmable-delay detonators, the delay time is programmed prior to blasting using a logger, programmer, or firing unit.
125th age 125qt year in the service to the Nation 2.3 2.4 3.0 3.1 3.2 3.3 3.4 3.5 3.6 3.7 4.0 Electronic detonators improves blasting safety, reduce ground vibrations, and.t enhance rock fragmentation during mining and infrastructure projects. They provide millisecond-level delay precision that older pyrotechnic or shock-tube systems cannot match, helping operations near civilian areas limit noise and flyrock. An electronic detonator is an initiation device in which the delay timing and firing are controlled by an electronic circuit or microchip that is activated by an appropriate electronic initiation signal or stimulus.
Subsequently, the standards prescribing the requirements, methods of sampling and tests of electronic detonators were developed and notified as IS 18462:2023.
The following guidelines to be followed & ensured for safe use of Permitted Electronic Detonator:
Permitted electronic detonators shall strictly conform in every respect with the construction, physical characteristics and other applicable requirements prescribed under IS 18462:2023 and the conditions specified in the relevant approval/test report. The e-Exploder shall be uniform in design and construction, and shall strictly conform to the technical and safety standards specified under IS 19359:2026.
The total electrical resistance of the circuit shall not be less than 1000 ohms and the short circuit capability of the logging equipment shall not be more than 50 mA.
The permitted electronic detonators intended for use in underground coal mines or metalliferous (where Regulation 142 of the MMR 1961 attracts) mines shall have adequate Gas Incendivity capability to prevent ignition.
The mechanical strength of lead-wires, connections, crimps and closures shall have adequate strength to prevent detonation, leading wire shall not break and pulled out from the shell during the handling & charging.
The detonators shall be packed substantially before delivery to the user and the user must keep detonators in their original packaging until immediately prior to use. The packing shall conform to the provisions of Explosives (Amendment) Rules, 2019.
Marking: Each package shall be marked with the following information:
a) Name, grade, type and strength of the material;
b) Number of pieces in the package;
c) Manufacturer's name and/or his recognized trade-mark, if any; and
d) Date of manufacture and lot number to enable the batch of manufacture to be traced from records.
(e)The marking shall further be in conformity to the provisions of Explosives (Amendment) Rules, 2019.
The cases of detonators of same grade, same type and belonging to the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.
The general conditions for use of Permitted Electronic Detonator and Electronic Exploder (Electronic Blasting System) shall be as follows:
age fr 125qi 125th year in the service to the Nation 4.1 4.2 4.3 4.4 5.0 5.1 5.2 6.0 6.1 6.2 6.3 In electronic blasting system, the initiation of permitted electronic detonator shall be done by using Electronic Exploder of same manufacturer and compatible with each other. In no case, initiation of permitted electronic detonators shall be done by the Electronic Exploder of another manufacturer.
The blasting/short-firing shall be conducted under the supervision of not below the rank of Overman Certificate of Competency (UR) under the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 or under the supervision prescribed as per the solid blasting conditions with respect to the degree of gassiness of the seam, whichever is more. In case of metalliferous mines not below the rank of Foreman Certificate of Competency (UR)
any other under the Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 or equivalent/corresponding certificate of competency.
Before using the electronic detonators, each detonator shall be subjected to the test for proper functioning using approved Electronic Exploder of same manufacturer.
Use approved loggers or testers to verifi/ network continuity and signal communication before arming.
Training: The users shall be trained in use of the e-Detonator in the field by supplier before its use in the mine, and regular maintenance of the e-Exploder shall be carried out by the trained Service Engineer and appointed & ensured by the manufacturer.
Persons engaged in use of the permitted electronic detonator & Electronic Exploder shall be suitably trained and duly authorized by the manager of the mine.
The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) shall be prepared for transport, storage, handling, charging, use and firing of permitted electronic detonator and the same shall be implemented during handling & use of the permitted electronic detonator and e-Exploder in the mine. Further, the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) shall be handed over to the concerned competent persons, supervisors and officials.
The following additional conditions shall also be maintained without deviation:
Manager shall maintain a copy of the instruction manual dealing with the methods of handling, care and limitations of use in the mine office and shall provide to the concerned persons.
Manager shall also maintain a copy of the extract of the conditions and special conditions, if any, recommended in the test report of the Permitted Electronic Detonator with regard to the safe handling and usage of Permitted Electronic Detonator and shall provide to the concerned persons.
All the conditions of the Solid Blasting permission of the concerned mine shall be complied with during the blasting operation.
fr 125Äi 125th year in the service to the Nation 6.4 6.5 6.6 6.7 7.0 Owner/Agent/Manager shall prepare site specific Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the handling and use of permitted electronic detonators and electronic .
exploders, and the same shall be strictly implemented during their use in the mine.
Any accident, injuries including loss of lives or properties caused due to defects or malfunctioning of this product shall be adequately indemnified by the manufacturer in agreement with the user (s) and such incidents shall be intimated to this Directorate.
All precautions in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 and Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 applicable for transport, storage, handling, charging, use and firing of the explosives in underground coal mines shall be observed.
Further, all operations using e-Detonator shall be carried out in strict compliance with the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017, Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 and the provisions notified under the OSH & WC Code, 2020 which includes subsequent amendments.
All the Owners/Agents/Managers are therefore advised to ensure strict compliance with the above guidelines while using permitted e-Exploder and e-Detonator in underground mines.

title: Guidelines for handling and use of e-Exploders in underground mines

BACKGROUND: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) had issued Gazette Notification No. S.O. 4255(E) dated 29thSeptember 2023, regarding the phased discontinuation of electric detonators concerning the issues of public safety and National security.
The government's assessment concluded the need for complete prohibition of electric detonator by the end of FY 2024—25.
Consequently, the mining and explosives industry is required to fully transition to electronic detonator (e-Detonator) and electronic exploder (e-Exploder) systems.
INTRODUCTION: An electronic exploder (e-Exploder) is a single device or a set of devices providing logging, continuity testing and blasting functions with authorisation to ensure safe use. These devices shall be used exclusively for communication with electronic detonators. It shall operate using a specific communication method and protocol compatible only with a corresponding type or model of electronic detonator designed using the same system architecture.
The standards for e-Detonator were developed and notified as IS 18462:2023 & the standards for e-Exploder were developed and notified as IS 19359:2026.
Subsequently, guidelines for testing standards of e-Exploder for use in underground mines were also notified through this Directorate's circular No. DGMS (Tech.)/ S&T/CircuIar(ApprovaI) No. 7, dated 14.08.2026.
Now, the following guidelines shall be followed for using Permitted Electronic Detonator in the mines:
Technical Specifications and Compliance Requirements for Electronic Exploders (e-ExpIoders): The e-Exploder shall be uniform in design and construction, and shall strictly conform to the technical and safety standards specified under IS 19359:2026. The e-Exploder shall be portable and robust enough to withstand the damp/complex mine environment and also equipped with a password-based authentication for issue of commands. It shall be capable of assessment of the healthiness of the detonator(s) which are connected in parallel.
The e-Exploder shall be so constructed that all parts have satisfactory strength, it shall have adequate insulation resistance and dielectric strength to withstand for a voltage of 250 volts. The enclosure case shall be robust such that it meets the requirements of drop test and impact test, splash proof and dust tightness (degree Of protection IP 54) in accordance with IS/IEC 60529:2001 (as amended time to time).
The enclosure of the permitted type e-Exploders shall be so constructed as not to give rise to ignition hazard of gas and coal dust due to frictional spark, static charges and leakage current in the third-degree gassy mines. The circuit of the e- Exploder shall be intrinsically safe conforming to IEC/IS: 60079-11:2023, as amended from time to time.
The health status of the electronic detonators shall be checked by using e-Exploder individually and collectively to confirm the continuity of each detonator before firing command /abort command. The e-Exploder shall be able to display the hole no and UID of the detonators that are not healthy or do not have continuity.
The e-Exploders shall have suitable arrangement to terminate the output energy pulse within four milliseconds of the release of the firing command/switch.
The e-Exploder shall facilitate the blasting operation from a safe distance as required under the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 and Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 and shall be intrinsically safe as approved by Director General Mines Safety (DGMS).
Training: The users shall be trained by manufacturer/supplier in the field before its use in the mine, and regular maintenance of the e-Exploder shall be carried out by the trained Service Engineer who appointed & ensured by the manufacturer.
Persons engaged in use of the permitted electronic detonator & Electronic Exploder in the mine shall be suitably trained and duly authorized by the manager of the mine.
It shall also be ensured that:

The e-Exploder shall be kept in a suitable box/case with caring straps in a lock & key and password protected, while using in the mines.
Electronic Exploder shall be operated by a removable key followed by authentication password for activation and other password for confirming fire command by the authorised Shotfirer/Blaster and he or she shall retain the e-Exploder key & password in his or her possession throughout the shift.
It shall be ensured that e-Detonator and e-Exploder of different makes are never connected together to prevent inadvertent initiation.
Testing of e-Exploder: shall be subjected to batch testing prior to use in mines at Government-approved / NABL-accredited laboratories (as per the DGMS e-Exploder guidelines or any modified/revised standards whichever is applicable), subject to confirmation of its accreditation granted by NABL for the relevant standard and that test house is not a part of any manufacturer's testing facility. Such testing shall cover peak open circuit voltage across output terminals of the e-Exploder, residual charge (which must be zero after 4 milliseconds), and duration of impulse current (which must be zero after 4 milliseconds of the firing command/switch). The Random samples shall be tested equivalent to 1% of the consignment or minimum one unit (whichever is higher).
Calibration of e-Exploder: The calibration for its resistance, impulse output current, circuit voltage and residual charge shall be done at every six (06) months and also calibrated after every repair or battery change The general conditions for use of Permitted Electronic Detonator and e-Exploder (Electronic Blasting System) shall be as follows:
The blasting/short-firing shall be conducted under the supervision of not below the rank of Overman Certificate of Competency (UR) under the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 or under the supervision as prescribed in the solid blasting conditions with respect to the degree of gassiness of the seam/mine, whoever is senior. In case of metalliferous mines not below the rank of Foreman Certificate of Competency (UR)

(a) Before using the electronic detonators, each detonator shall be subjected to the test for proper functioning using approved e-Exploder of same manufacturer.
(b) All the conditions of the solid blasting permission of the concerned seam of the mine shall be complied with during the blasting operation.
The details of each blasting shall be recorded in a bound paged book & signed by the competent person, who conducted the blasting, which shall be countersigned by the Assistant Manager and Manager of the mine.
The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) shall be prepared for transport, storage, handling, charging, use and firing of permitted electronic detonator & e-Exploder and the same shall be implemented during handling & use of the permitted electronic detonator and e-Exploder in the mine. Further, the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) shall be handed over to the concerned competent persons, supervisors and officials.
The test report on "short circuit test" of e-Exploder shall be conducted and maintained as per the guidelines mentioned in IS 19359:2026.
The e-exploder shall not be used after its self-life as prescribed by the manufacturer.
The defective and malfunction e-Exploder shall be tagged with "NOT IN WORKING ORDER" and it shall not be used for firing of shots.
All precautions in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017 and Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 applicable for transport, storage, handling, charging, use and firing of the explosives in underground coal/metalliferous mines shall be observed.
Further, all other operations using e-Exploder shall be carried out in strict compliance with the Coal Mines Regulations, 2017, Metalliferous Mines Regulations, 1961 and the provisions notified under the OSH & WC Code, 2020 which includes subsequent amendments.
All the Owners/Agents/Managers are therefore advised to ensure strict compliance with the above guidelines while using permitted e-Exploder and -Detonator in underground mines.
